To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antisite arsenics concentration is dependent on the growth parameters such as arsenic flux, substrate temperature, and growth rates and that it saturates beyond a certain critical flux.
the antisite As incorporation in the low-temperature MBE of GaAs is dependent on arsenic flux, substrate temperature, and growth conditions.
the incorporation of antiside As is a surface kinetic process that depends on the arsenic flux, substrate temperature, and growth conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics and modeling of the incorporation of antisites in the low temperature (LT) MBE of GaAs.
the modeling of the surface growth processes and incorporation of AsGa in the low temperature growth of GaAs by MBE.
the physics of the low temperature MOCVD of gallium arsenides and the modeling of the growth dynamics of gallium arsenic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antisite arsenics concentration increases with the arsenic flux and decreases with the substrate temperature.
the AsGa concentration is a function of the growth temperature, arsenic flux, and growth rate.

the antisite arsenics concentration is a function of temperature, growth rate, and arsenic flux and the activation energy of the evaporation of the antisite AsGa is about 1.16eV and the frequency factor is 4×1011/s.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the developed model is a powerful tool in understanding the growth kinetics in the low temperature growth of GaAs and in predicting the AsGa concentration in the grown material for a wide range of growth conditions.
the antisite As concentration in GaAs can be controlled to a large extent by the arsenic flux and substrate temperature.
the antisite As incorporation is an intrinsic property of GaAs growth and is independent of the growth conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AsGa incorporation in the MBE of GaAs is not an intrinsic property of GaAs and can be controlled by the growth conditions.
the incorporation of AsGa can be minimized by using low arsenic flux, high growth rates and high temperatures.
the incorporation of AsGa is not only dependent on the arsenic flux but also on the growth rate and substrate temperature.
